title: Bushels Held Back in Store Against the Grade Guarantee
content:
Bushels are held back for grade, because what goes out has to leave enough behind to make good what the elevator guaranteed. This rule governs releases out of store under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Standing rule

Where a grade discount has been raised on the account in the last twelve months and the agreement carries no bushels pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt, the wide grade holdback of 900 bushels stays in store, the whole of that exposure riding on what is left standing in store.

Where a grade discount has been raised on the account in the last twelve months and the agreement carries bushels pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt, the light grade holdback of 400 bushels stays in store, the receipt already keeping a margin standing for the same grade.

And otherwise, no grade discount having been raised on the account in the last twelve months, nothing is held back for grade.

## Condition and result

| A grade discount raised on the account in the last twelve months | Bushels pledged against an outstanding warehouse receipt | Held back in store |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | 900 |
| yes | some | 400 |
| no | none | nothing |
| no | some | nothing |

Where no grade discount has been raised within the twelve months, whether anything stands pledged makes no difference at all.

## Worked holdbacks, on hypothetical accounts

**An account carrying a grade discount raised five months ago, with nothing pledged on the agreement.** The wide holdback of 900 bushels stays in store.

**The same account with 3000 bushels pledged against an outstanding receipt.** The light holdback of 400 bushels stays in store.

**An account whose most recent grade discount was raised nineteen months ago, with nothing pledged.** The discount falls outside the twelve months, so nothing is held back for grade.
